intro: A bedazzled switch plate is one of the smallest changes you can make to a rental, and it works best in rooms where the walls are plain and the light switch is in your line of sight. Before you buy, check what kind of switch you have, since toggles, rockers and dimmers each need a plate sized for them. Turn off the breaker before you remove the old plate, and keep the original plate and screws so you can swap them back before your lease ends. Most people start with a bedroom or hallway, then add more once they like the look.

picks.description: A silver rhinestone toggle cover is the simplest way to add sparkle to a plain wall. It fits a standard single toggle switch, so you swap one plastic plate for one bedazzled plate and keep the original screws in a labeled bag. Silver stones match most paint colors, from white walls to dark accent colors, and they catch light from a lamp without looking loud. The stones are glued in place, so dust them with a dry brush rather than spraying them with cleaner. Check the plate size against your switch before you order, because toggle and rocker plates are not interchangeable. Once the breaker is off, the swap takes about ten minutes per switch. A hallway switch is a good first project because it is seen often and touched lightly.
picks.best_for: Renters wanting a quick, classic glam upgrade in a hallway or bedroom
picks.quirky_fact: Silver rhinestones reflect more light than clear crystals in a dim room, which is why a small plate can look brighter than it is.
picks.shop_query: silver rhinestone toggle light switch cover
picks.skip_if: You need a plate for a rocker or dimmer, since this fits toggles only
picks.product_name: Silver rhinestone toggle light switch cover

picks.description: A rose gold crystal rocker plate suits apartments with warm tones, cream walls and soft textiles. Rocker switches are the large flat switches that many newer rentals use, and this plate covers the full rectangle so the switch looks finished. Rose gold pairs well with brass hardware and wood furniture, and it looks softer than bright silver. Before you buy, check that the plate matches a single rocker, since a double rocker needs a two-gang plate. Clean the stones with a dry brush and avoid pressing hard on the plate, because the crystals can loosen over time. The plate takes about fifteen minutes to fit once the power is off. Keep the original plastic plate in a bag so you can swap it back when you move.
picks.best_for: Warm-toned rentals with rocker switches and soft, neutral decor
picks.quirky_fact: Rose gold is a copper and gold alloy, so its color shifts depending on the light in the room.
picks.shop_query: rose gold crystal rocker switch plate
picks.skip_if: Your switch is a standard toggle, since this plate is sized for a rocker
picks.product_name: Rose gold crystal rocker switch plate

picks.breed: Faux Pearl and Diamond Switch Plate
picks.description: A faux pearl and diamond switch plate fits the coquette, grandmillennial and vintage looks that are popular in bedrooms and small sitting rooms. Faux pearls in a row with small clear diamonds make a soft, romantic border around the switch. The plate looks best in a room with floral wallpaper or lace textiles, and it can clash with bold modern art. Check the plate size against your switch before you order, since toggles and rockers use different frames. Pearls are glued or set into the plate, so avoid cleaning them with wet cloths. The swap is simple: turn off the breaker, remove the old plate, fit the new one and tighten the screws gently. A bedroom light switch is a good place to start because you see it at the same time each evening.
picks.best_for: Bedrooms and vintage-style rooms that need a romantic accent
picks.quirky_fact: Faux pearls are usually made from glass or resin coated in a layer that imitates the glow of a natural pearl.
picks.shop_query: faux pearl diamond light switch cover
picks.skip_if: Your room has a modern, minimal look that the pearls would clash with
picks.product_name: Faux pearl and diamond light switch cover

picks.description: A black rhinestone dimmer plate gives a moody, dark look to a bedroom, a home office or a dark accent wall. Black stones absorb more light than clear ones, so the plate reads as a bold shape rather than a sparkle. It works best with dark or jewel-toned walls and with dark wood or metal furniture. Dimmer switches have a knob or slider, so the plate needs a cutout sized for it. Check your dimmer's size before ordering, since a standard toggle plate will not fit. Clean the stones with a dry brush, and keep the plate away from direct sunlight if the rhinestones are glued on, since heat can soften some adhesives. Installing the plate takes about fifteen minutes with the breaker off.
picks.best_for: Dark-walled rooms and dimmer switches that need a bold, moody accent
picks.quirky_fact: Black rhinestones are often coated on the back with a dark foil, which is why they look darker than clear crystals in daylight.
picks.skip_if: Your room is very bright and you want the switch to read as sparkly

picks.description: An iridescent AB crystal switch cover flashes a rainbow shimmer as light moves across it. AB stands for aurora borealis, a coating that gives crystals a shifting color effect. It suits a room with a single lamp or a window with changing daylight, since the color changes through the day. The cover is a good choice for a kids room or a teen bedroom, where a playful look fits. Choose a plate sized for your switch, and check that the crystals sit flush so the plate does not catch on clothing. Clean with a dry brush and avoid rubbing the crystals, which can wear the coating over time. The swap takes about ten minutes once the power is off, and the original plate can be stored for the next move.
picks.best_for: Teen rooms and anyone who wants a playful, color-shifting accent
picks.quirky_fact: AB coatings were first developed for crystal glassware, and they are now used on rhinestones and switch covers for a rainbow effect.
picks.skip_if: You want a calm, neutral look that will not draw the eye

picks.description: A crushed diamond mirrored switch plate is a practical choice for a small, dark rental. The mirrored finish reflects lamplight and daylight from the room, which can make a dim corner feel brighter. The plate works in a hallway or a small bathroom where a single switch is the only fixture. Mirrored plates show fingerprints more than rhinestone plates, so wipe them with a dry microfiber cloth. Check the plate size before buying, since mirrored covers are sold for toggles, rockers and dimmers. The swap is simple with the breaker off. Avoid placing the plate near a steamy shower or a stove, where moisture or heat can damage the finish. A mirror plate is also easy to match with other silver or chrome fittings in the room.
picks.best_for: Small, dim rooms that need reflected light without a new fixture
picks.quirky_fact: Mirror finishes on switch plates are usually a thin metallic coating, so they reflect light most strongly when the plate sits flat.
picks.skip_if: You want a soft, low-shine finish or the room gets very humid

picks.description: A gold glitter and gemstone switch plate is a maximalist choice for people who like bold color and texture. A chunky gold glitter base with colored gemstones makes the switch a focal point rather than a background detail. It suits a room with other gold accents, such as lamps or picture frames, and a neutral wall color that lets the plate stand out. Glitter can shed onto fabric, so wipe the plate with a dry cloth and keep it away from bedding where possible. Choose a size that matches your switch, and check that the gemstones are glued firmly before you install. The plate takes about fifteen minutes to fit once the breaker is off. Keep the original plastic plate in storage so you can change it back when your tastes shift.
picks.best_for: Maximalist rooms and anyone who wants bold gold texture on a switch
picks.quirky_fact: Gold glitter is usually made from polyester film coated in metal, which is why it holds its shine better than natural metallic dust.
picks.skip_if: You prefer minimal decor or have a glitter-sensitive household
picks.product_name: Gold glitter and gemstone light switch plate

picks.description: A subtle crystal border switch cover gives a small amount of sparkle without covering the whole plate. A thin row of clear crystals runs around the edge, and the center stays plain. It is the safest option for a renter who wants a touch of glam but does not want the switch to dominate the wall. It suits any room color, from white to deep green, and works well in a shared hallway. Check the plate size and border style before you buy, since some borders are sized for a toggle and others for a rocker. Clean the crystals with a dry brush, and avoid pressing the border with your fingers, since the crystals can loosen. Installation takes about ten minutes once the power is off.
picks.best_for: Renters who want a light touch of sparkle in a shared or formal space
picks.quirky_fact: Crystal borders are often set using a row of small prongs, which is why they stay in place without much adhesive.
picks.skip_if: You want the switch to be a bold focal point rather than a quiet detail
picks.product_name: Subtle crystal border light switch cover

picks.description: An emerald green jewel switch plate brings a rich, jewel-toned color to a room with white or cream walls. Colored rhinestones in deep green look more luxurious than clear crystals, and the color pairs well with brass, velvet and dark wood. The plate suits a living room, dining room or bedroom where green is already part of the palette. Check the size before buying, since jewel plates are sold for each switch type. Clean with a dry brush, and keep the plate away from heat, since some colored glue can soften. Green rhinestones can look darker under warm bulbs, so test the color in your room before committing to several plates. The swap takes about fifteen minutes with the breaker off.
picks.best_for: Rooms with green or brass accents that need a rich jewel tone
picks.quirky_fact: Emerald-colored stones have been a popular jewelry tone for centuries, and the same deep green now appears on home decor.
picks.skip_if: Your room has strong green or red walls that the plate would blend into
picks.product_name: Emerald green rhinestone light switch plate

picks.description: A pink rhinestone double toggle cover adds a playful, bold color to a room with two switches side by side. Double toggle plates cover two switches with one plate, which is useful in a kitchen or a bedroom where a pair of switches sits by the door. Bright pink suits a teen bedroom, a dorm-style room or a home with a bold color palette. Check that the plate is sized for two toggles before buying, since a single-toggle plate will not cover both. Pink stones can fade in strong sunlight, so keep the plate out of direct sun if you can. Clean with a dry brush, and remove the plate carefully before moving so the stones do not catch on fabric or cords. The swap is quick once the breaker is off.
picks.best_for: Bold, playful rooms and double-toggle switch pairs
picks.quirky_fact: Pink rhinestones are often made with a colored glass base, so the color stays consistent even when the plate is cleaned often.
picks.skip_if: You want a neutral look or your switches are single rockers
picks.product_name: Pink rhinestone double toggle light switch cover

faqs.question: Are bedazzled light switch covers safe to use?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the base of the switch plate is made from non-conductive plastic or properly insulated metal. Turn off the power at the breaker before you remove the old plate, and check with a voltage tester that the wires are dead. Make sure the new plate matches your switch type and sits flat against the wall. If you are not comfortable working with wiring, a licensed electrician can change the plate in a few minutes.

faqs.question: How do I clean a rhinestone light switch cover?
faqs.answer: Avoid spraying liquid cleaners directly onto the rhinestones, because moisture can loosen the glue. Use a clean, dry, soft-bristled brush or a microfiber cloth to remove dust from between the stones. For fingerprints on a smooth surface, a barely damp cloth works, but dry the plate right away. Check the plate every few months, since rhinestones can loosen in high-traffic areas like a hallway.

faqs.question: Can I take my glam switch plates when I move out?
faqs.answer: Yes. That is one reason they suit renters. Remove the decorative plate, put the original plastic plate back on, and store the bedazzled plate and its screws in a labeled bag. Check your lease first, since some landlords want all fixtures left as they were. Keep the original screws, because the new plate may use a different length.

faqs.question: Do these covers fit all types of light switches?
faqs.answer: You need to match the cover to your switch type. The most common are standard toggles, the small switch that flips up and down, and rocker plates, the large flat rectangular switches. Dimmers need a plate sized for a dimmer knob, and double switches need a two-gang plate. Measure your current plate and count the switches before you order, because a plate sized for one switch will not fit a two-switch box.

answer: A silver rhinestone toggle cover, a rose gold crystal rocker plate and a faux pearl and diamond switch plate are the three easiest ways to add glam without changing the wall. Each one is a single-gang plate that goes on in a few minutes once the power is off. The deciding factor is the switch type: a toggle needs a toggle plate, and a rocker needs a rocker plate.
